blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Autoregressive language models produce, at every prediction step, a vocabulary-sized logit vector whose structure determines the conditional next-token distribution. We empirically identify that the ordered vocabulary-head logits follow a remarkably consistent log-linear relation
  \[ z_{(r)} \approx μ- α\log r. \] across prediction contexts, architectures, and scales, emerging progressively during pretraining. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic analysis of the logit geometry underlying the distributional assumptions used in the prior decoding work. While controlled order-statistic baselines spanning bounded, light-tailed, and heavier-tailed distributions can largely explain the observed log-linear geometry, they do not explain the systematic shift in the slope $α$: trained language models exhibit $α\approx 1.4$--$1.7$, sitting well above the initialization baseline ($α\approx 0.2$) . Moreover, $α$ correlates with predictive performance, suggesting that it captures learned structure beyond generic extreme-value effects.

\[z_{(r)]\相近 μ- α\log r.\] 跨越预测背景,结构和尺度,在预训期间逐渐出现. 据我们所知,这是对先前解码工作所使用的分配假设所依据的对数几何进行的第一次系统分析。 虽然控制有序的统计基线跨越界限、轻尾和较重的尾部分布大致可以解释所观察到的对数线几何,但它们不能解释坡度的系统变化:训练有素的语言模型显示大约为1.4-1.7美元,远远高于初始化基线(约0.2美元)。 此外,美元与预测性能有关,表明它捕捉到超出一般极端价值效应的学习出的结构。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: At every prediction step, an autoregressive language model assigns a score to every token in its vocabulary, which governs how probability mass is distributed over possible continuations. Sampling is the last step of generation; the logits are where the real decision is already made. While substantial work has studied the resulting token probabilities, generated text, and hidden representations, the structure of this vocabulary-wide logit vector remains comparatively unexplored.
blocks.zh: 在每一个预测步骤中,自相递减的语言模型都会给词汇中的每一个符号分配一个分数,这个分数规范概率质量如何被分配到可能的续作上. 采样是生成的最后一步;对数是真正的决定已经作出的地方。 虽然大量的工作研究了由此产生的符号概率、生成的文本和隐藏的表示,但这种全词汇的逻辑矢量的结构仍然比较没有加以探讨。

blocks.en: One natural way to expose this structure is to ignore token identities and examine the logits in rank order. This perspective is also directly relevant to common decoding procedures, such as top- k k and top- p p sampling, which operate on the vocabulary head by selecting or truncating the highest-ranked logits. This leads to a simple question: Does the ordered logit vector possess a simple geometric structure?
blocks.zh: 揭露这种结构的一个自然方式是忽略象征身份,按等级顺序检查日志. 这种视角也与常见的解码程序直接相干,如top-k k和top-p sample,它们通过选择或截取排名最高的日志来操作词汇头. 这导致一个简单的问题: 命令的对数向量是否具有简单的几何结构?

blocks.en: We empirically find a remarkably regular structure in the vocabulary head: ordered logits follow an approximately log-linear relation across prediction contexts, architectures, and model scales, and this structure emerges during pretraining. This raises the question of how much of this structure is attributable to language models and how much arises generically from order statistics.
blocks.zh: 我们从经验中发现词汇头有一个非常正常的结构: 命令的对数在预测背景、架构和模型尺度之间 遵循一个大致的对数线性关系, 这种结构在预训期间出现。 这就提出了这样一个问题:这种结构有多少可归结于语言模型,从秩序统计中一般产生多少。

blocks.en: Controlled order-statistic baselines show that ranking any finite collection of random variables induces its own structure, and light-tailed distributions can produce approximately log-linear ordered spectra. We therefore focus on the spectral slope α \alpha , examining how it differs from generic baselines, how it varies across models, and what information it carries about the model’s predictive state.
blocks.zh: 受控的顺序-统计基线显示,任何有限收集的随机变量的排名都会诱发自己的结构,而光尾分布可以产生大约对数线被订购的光谱. 因此,我们专注于光谱坡 α-α, 研究它与一般基线的区别, 模型之间的差别, 以及模型的预测状态。

blocks.en:
Our contributions are: (i) We characterize a consistent log-linear geometry in the ordered
vocabulary-head logits of autoregressive language models across contexts,
architectures, scales, and training. (ii) We distinguish generic order-statistic geometry from learned
structure using controlled distributional baselines, identifying the spectral
slope α \alpha as the key empirical distinction between the regimes. (iii) We show that the spectral distribution can be efficiently reconstructed from the vocabulary head and that α \alpha correlates with pre-hoc predictive
uncertainty (entropy) and post-hoc prediction quality, measured by NLL,
ground-truth token probability p true p_{\mathrm{true}} , and ground-truth token
rank.

blocks.en:
Our results reveal two complementary aspects of the ordered logit spectrum.
Approximately log-linear geometry can arise generically from order statistics,

approximately reconstruct the ranked
probability spectrum. This compact structure may provide a basis for approximating vocabulary-sized predictive distributions without
retaining the full spectrum. Moreover, α \alpha systematically tracks aspects of the model’s predictive state, providing a compact summary of variation in next-token
predictions.

Zipf’s law describes corpus-level token frequencies aggregated over natural

object of study is different: we analyze the model’s predicted logit vector
for each individual prediction context, before any token is sampled. The
resulting log-linear law is therefore a pre-hoc property of conditional
predictions rather than a post-hoc property of natural or generated text.
